title: CO2 Recovery Time After Occupancy
app: Raspberry Shake, Safecast, Blitzortung-compatible lightning sensors, AirGradient CO2 sensors, radon monitors, allsky cameras, and magnetometers streamed to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=airgradient:sensor
| stats avg(recovery_min) as avg_recovery_min, max(recovery_min) as max_recovery_min by room
| where avg_recovery_min>45 OR max_recovery_min>90
| sort - avg_recovery_min
description: Uses AirGradient room telemetry telemetry to monitor how quickly rooms recover after people leave in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for spaces that ventilate too slowly after occupancy, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest AirGradient room telemetry data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
visualization: Room table of average and max CO2 recovery time.
grandmaExplanation: It celebrates how quickly rooms recover after people leave so you can spot spaces that ventilate too slowly after occupancy before it becomes annoying.
